summary: Serverless/BaaS architecture: Supabase serving React Native (Expo) for Android, hosted on Supabase managed platform (ap-south-1 Mumbai). Estimated $25-100/month (within the $100 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: Supabase provides data, auth and APIs as managed services; custom logic runs as functions, so there is no server fleet to operate. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 2 engineer(s), no DevOps cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Mobile - React Native (Expo): Chosen because team already works in javascript (team.languages); strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=4; on-device SQLite storage and background sync for offline_support=true; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=5.

alternatives.choice: Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (native Android) for Android
alternatives.why_not: No kotlin/java in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk. React Native scores higher on time-to-market and learning curve (fit 5.6 vs 8.2).
No dart in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk. React Native scores higher on time-to-market and learning curve (fit 5.2 vs 8.2).

tradeoffs: JS runtime overhead on very low-end phones (Hermes mitigates)
Some native modules need custom development builds

backend.justification: Chosen because team already works in javascript (team.languages); strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=5; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=4; BaaS covers auth, data and storage without writing server code. Accepted trade-off: supabase.co was ISP-blocked in India in Feb 2026; needs a custom domain.

alternatives.why_not: Sync batches and large uploads run into function time/size limits. Supabase scores higher on fit for the project type and time-to-market (fit 8.9 vs 9.0).
Supabase scores higher on fit for the project type and cost (fit 7.7 vs 9.0).
Excluded by hard constraint: its Authentication product has no data-location choice (infrastructure.data_residency).

tradeoffs: Complex workflows end up in Edge Functions or SQL functions
supabase.co was ISP-blocked in India in Feb 2026 (a custom domain mitigates)

database.justification: Chosen because Supabase is built on PostgreSQL; strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=4; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=5. Managed as Supabase Postgres: the Supabase project's own Postgres; same platform and private network as the application hosting.

alternatives.why_not: Would bypass the Supabase data model. PostgreSQL on Supabase Postgres scores higher on maintainability and security (fit -0.6 vs 12.3).
Would bypass the Supabase data model. PostgreSQL on Supabase Postgres scores higher on maintainability and cost (fit -1.4 vs 12.3).
Supabase already includes Postgres. Supabase Postgres scores higher on integration with the hosting platform (fit -6.4 vs 8.3).
Excluded by hard constraint: no India region (infrastructure.data_residency=india).

tradeoffs: Single-writer primary: write scale beyond one large node needs partitioning/sharding
Vacuum and connection pooling need attention at scale

hosting.justification: The Android app talks directly to Supabase (database, auth, storage and functions are all managed in ap-south-1 Mumbai), so there is no web tier or server to host.

alternatives.why_not: Only needed once custom server code outgrows the BaaS's edge functions; today it would be a deployment target with nothing to deploy.

warnings.message: supabase.co was blocked by several Indian ISPs in Feb 2026 (since restored). Serve the API on your own custom domain so clients never depend on supabase.co DNS.
CERT-In Directions (2022): keep ICT system logs for 180 days within Indian jurisdiction.
DPDP Act 2023: consent notices, purpose limitation, breach intimation to the Data Protection Board and erasure on request. India residency is enforced because data_residency=india.
Offline writes need a conflict policy: client-generated UUIDs, server-authoritative merge or per-field last-write-wins, and idempotent sync endpoints.

assumptions: requirements.p95_latency_ms is null: no latency-driven selection applied (interactive apps assume ~500 ms is acceptable)
